extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and practitioners working on sarcasm detection and dataset curation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and dataset description for creating/using a news-headline dataset for sarcasm detection (curated from satirical and real news sources). Focuses on source selection, label reliability, size, and extensibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hashtag-based supervision for Twitter datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: “Past studies in Sarcasm Detection mostly make use of Twitter datasets collected using hashtag-based supervision but such datasets are noisy in terms of labels and language.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on hashtag-based signals to label sarcasm because they produce noisy labels and noisy language. Prefer alternative sources or stronger labeling procedures to improve label quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for context when tweets are replies
rubrics_metrics.description: “Many tweets are replies to other tweets, and detecting sarcasm in these requires the availability of contextual tweets.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using tweets, ensure conversational/contextual context is available for items that are replies, otherwise exclude replies or annotate/collect surrounding context to enable correct sarcasm interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curate from complementary sources: satirical vs real news
rubrics_metrics.description: “We curate News Headlines Dataset from two news websites: TheOnion aims at producing sarcastic versions of current events, whereas HuffPost publishes real news.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select source domains with clear distinctions (e.g., a satirical outlet for sarcastic examples and a mainstream news outlet for non-sarcastic examples) to create more reliable class labels based on provenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide dataset size and class composition
rubrics_metrics.description: “The dataset contains about 28K headlines out of which 13K are sarcastic.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report total example counts and class breakdowns so users can assess scale and class balance; aim for sizable collections (tens of thousands) for robust model training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include source links to enable extensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: “To make it more useful, we have included the source links of the news articles so that more data can be extracted as needed.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish provenance (URLs/IDs) alongside items so downstream users can retrieve full articles, metadata, or additional context; this increases the dataset's reusability for other tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer cleaner domains (news headlines) to reduce noise
rubrics_metrics.description: “To overcome the limitations related to noise in Twitter datasets, we curate News Headlines Dataset ...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, choose domains with less colloquial/noisy language (e.g., curated news headlines vs social media posts) to reduce label and language noise in sarcasm datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document dataset details and potential use cases
rubrics_metrics.description: “In this paper, we describe various details about the dataset and potential use cases apart from Sarcasm Detection.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comprehensive documentation (collection methodology, labeling assumptions, limitations) and example use cases to facilitate correct application and secondary uses beyond the original task.
